events.title: Pompey celebrates his third triumph
events.description: Pompey the Great celebrated his third triumph, for his victories over the pirates and the end of the Mithridatic Wars, on his 45th birthday. The settlement of 63 BCE had seen Rome annex Pontus and Syria.
events.html: Pompey the Great celebrated his third triumph, for his victories over the pirates and the end of the Mithridatic Wars, on his 45th birthday. The settlement of 63 BCE had seen Rome annex Pontus and Syria.

events.title: Leo I, later called Leo the Great, becomes Bishop of Rome
events.description: Leo was consecrated as Bishop of Rome after the death of Sixtus III on 18 August 440. He held the office for more than twenty years, until his death on 10 November 461, and came to be known as Leo the Great.
events.html: Leo was consecrated as Bishop of Rome after the death of Sixtus III on 18 August 440. He held the office for more than twenty years, until his death on 10 November 461, and came to be known as Leo the Great.

events.title: Pope Benedict III is restored by a popular uprising
events.description: After Louis II of Italy, Carolingian emperor, tried to replace him with his own favoured candidate, Benedict III was restored to the papacy by a popular uprising. He reigned as bishop of Rome until his death in April 858.
events.html: After Louis II of Italy, Carolingian emperor, tried to replace him with his own favoured candidate, Benedict III was restored to the papacy by a popular uprising. He reigned as bishop of Rome until his death in April 858.

events.title: Pope Gregory IX excommunicates Emperor Frederick II
events.description: Gregory IX excommunicated Frederick II for again delaying his promised crusade. Frederick went anyway, regaining Jerusalem by treaty in 1229 and crowning himself in the Holy Sepulchre.
events.html: Gregory IX excommunicated Frederick II for again delaying his promised crusade. Frederick went anyway, regaining Jerusalem by treaty in 1229 and crowning himself in the Holy Sepulchre.

events.title: Henry III recognises Llywelyn ap Gruffudd as Prince of Wales
events.description: In the Treaty of Montgomery, Henry III recognised Llywelyn ap Gruffudd as Prince of Wales, with overlordship of the other Welsh lords, in return for homage and a large payment. Disputes over these led to Edward I's invasion of 1277.
events.html: In the Treaty of Montgomery, Henry III recognised Llywelyn ap Gruffudd as Prince of Wales, with overlordship of the other Welsh lords, in return for homage and a large payment. Disputes over these led to Edward I's invasion of 1277.

events.title: Anglo-Breton forces win the Battle of Auray
events.description: At Auray, Anglo-Breton forces defeated the Franco-Breton army in the decisive battle of the War of the Breton Succession, the struggle between the counts of Blois and the Montforts for the Duchy of Brittany. The war ended the following April.
events.html: At Auray, Anglo-Breton forces defeated the Franco-Breton army in the decisive battle of the War of the Breton Succession, the struggle between the counts of Blois and the Montforts for the Duchy of Brittany. The war ended the following April.

events.title: An earthquake ruins much of Antigua Guatemala
events.description: An earthquake of an estimated magnitude of 7.4 destroyed much of the architecture of Antigua Guatemala, then the colonial capital of Central America, ruining over 3,000 buildings. The authorities considered moving the seat of government to a safer place.

events.title: Horatio Nelson is born in Norfolk
events.description: Horatio Nelson was born at Burnham Thorpe, the son of a rector. He won the battles of the Nile and Copenhagen and died at his greatest victory, Trafalgar, in 1805.
events.html: Horatio Nelson was born at Burnham Thorpe, the son of a rector. He won the battles of the Nile and Copenhagen and died at his greatest victory, Trafalgar, in 1805.

events.title: London's Metropolitan Police go on patrol for the first time
events.description: Constables of Robert Peel's new Metropolitan Police began patrolling London. Nicknamed 'Bobbies' or 'Peelers', they set a model of uniformed, civilian policing by consent.
events.html: Constables of Robert Peel's new Metropolitan Police began patrolling London. Nicknamed 'Bobbies' or 'Peelers', they set a model of uniformed, civilian policing by consent.

events.title: Munich conference hands the Sudetenland to Germany
events.description: Chamberlain, Daladier, Hitler and Mussolini agreed at Munich that Czechoslovakia must cede the Sudetenland; the deal was signed after midnight. Czechoslovakia was not consulted.

song: It's a Long Way to Tipperary
English music hall; British and Empire soldiers of the First World War
A music hall song of an Irishman in London missing home. British soldiers sang it as they marched to the First World War.
